page.title: Offers
page.purpose: Show the offer graph and let an operator understand and change one offer's state. The graph view carries a table equivalent so it is usable without sight and without a pointer.

priorities.statement: This offer's current state, and what it is waiting on
Which transitions are legal from here — and, on refusal, which rule refused and why
The trigger in the form it was declared, and the facts it reads
History: who changed what, when, and why

states.description: The surface at rest with data present — the state a journey step assumes when it names none.
Nothing in flight; the surface is at rest and its controls are usable.
A user-triggered operation is in flight and its outcome is not yet known.
An operation completed; the result is announced, not merely rendered.
First read of the surface's data; layout is reserved so nothing shifts on arrival.
A write is in flight; the affected control is disabled and says why.
A background read is refreshing data the user is already looking at.
A user-requested re-read of data already on screen.
The query succeeded and there is genuinely nothing — distinct from not-yet-loaded.
Some contributing source could not be read; what is missing is named.
Displayed data is older than its freshness window; its age is shown.
Input was rejected before submission; the offending field is identified.
The request failed; the reason and the next action are stated.
An automatic retry is in progress; attempt count and next attempt are visible.
The caller's role does not permit this; what role would is stated.
The client cannot reach the API; queued or read-only behavior is explained.
An illegal transition was attempted. The refusal names the rule and the legal alternatives; the offer's state is unchanged.
The append-only audit trail for one offer is open, showing actor, timestamp, prior value and reason for every state change.
A non-operator actor attempted the transition to active. It is refused as a permission, naming the role that would be required.
A deliverable this offer claims does not exist in the live deliverable set. Reported as a finding on the offer rather than silently dropped from the membership list.
An operator compares two same-kind records, sees the references that will move and any edge collapse, and explicitly confirms the audited merge.
The offers route opens in a grouped catalog view with node counts by kind and edge counts on every node.
The grouped catalog has no nodes and explains how to create the first record; the flat table remains reachable.
A grouped catalog contains a node with no relationships and says so rather than implying missing data is connected.
Catalog verification reports duplicate identities and the grouped view shows a blocking banner with the count.

claims.statement: The offer graph is accompanied by a table carrying the same nodes and edges.
claims.rationale: PRD accessibility rule and DESIGN.md: a directed graph is unusable without sight or a pointer, and the graph is not the information — only one rendering of it.

claims.statement: A refused transition states which rule refused it and what would satisfy that rule.
claims.rationale: OT-P0-002 and the PRD voice rule. A refusal with no remedy converts an enforced lifecycle into an obstacle, which is how enforcement gets removed later.

claims.statement: The append-only audit trail for an offer — actor, timestamp, prior value, reason — is reachable from the offer.
claims.rationale: OT-P0-007. The trail is the only evidence of who promoted what; with no surface it cannot be checked by the person it protects.

claims.statement: A non-operator attempt to promote is refused as a permission, naming the role that would be required.
claims.rationale: OT-P0-005. The source canon said 'agents never self-promote' as an instruction; presenting the refusal as a permission rather than an error is what makes the boundary legible.

claims.statement: An offer in a waiting state shows the declared trigger it is waiting on and the facts that trigger reads.
claims.rationale: Priority 1. An offer parked with no visible condition is exactly the forgotten-candidate failure the scenario exists to end.

claims.statement: The transitions that are legal from the current state are shown, rather than discovered by attempting one.
claims.rationale: Priority 2. Discovery-by-refusal trains the operator to treat refusals as noise.

claims.statement: Every offer status carries a text label rather than relying on a status tint.
claims.rationale: PRD accessibility rule: status is the single most consequential thing on any surface in this scenario.

claims.statement: A deliverable an offer claims but which does not exist is shown as a finding on the offer, not omitted from the list.
claims.rationale: OT-P1-001. Silently dropping a dangling member makes the membership list look correct while it is wrong — the same class of failure as reporting a missing figure as zero.

claims.statement: Offer authoring forms expose their submit actions as real keyboard-operable controls.
The offer promotion control is keyboard reachable.
The duplicate merge surface names the survivor, duplicate, reference counts, collapsed edges, confirmation, cancellation, and completion feedback.
claims.rationale: GRAPH-005: deleting a duplicate is allowed only when the operator sees which identity survives, what moves, and what audit record will remain.

claims.statement: The offer surface renders the board's rank reason as text, including named actuals unavailability rather than a fabricated zero.
The default grouped catalog shows a node count for each kind and edge counts by kind for each node.
claims.rationale: A flat row list hides the shape of the repaired graph; counts make identity and relationship coverage visible at a glance.

claims.statement: The operator can switch from the grouped catalog to the existing flat table.
claims.rationale: Grouping is a default projection, not a replacement for the searchable record table.

claims.statement: A duplicate-identity banner appears when verification reports duplicates and is absent when verification is reconciled.
claims.rationale: The banner makes the exact defect class that caused the repair visible without turning a clean catalog into an alarm.
